chunks: And with this chain of transmission:
That Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought a man who had snatched a pearl from the ear of a slave-girl, and he said:
This is open insolence; so he struck him and imprisoned him.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام as leader of the faithful
key_terms.اخْتَلَسَ: he snatched or took furtively and suddenly
key_terms.الْإِسْنَادِ: the chain of narrators transmitting the report
key_terms.جَارِيَةٍ: a slave-girl from whose ear the pearl was taken
key_terms.دُرَّةً: a pearl taken as the object of theft
key_terms.فَضَرَبَهُ: so he struck him, indicating disciplinary punishment

ai.seo_question: How did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام judge a person who openly snatched a pearl from a girl’s ear?
ai.summary: This report describes a legal judgment of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding a person who openly snatched property from a girl’s ear. The act is treated as a manifest offense warranting disciplinary punishment and imprisonment, reflecting judicial handling of public theft-like misconduct distinct from the fixed hadd of formal theft.
